answer: One concrete defense is stake-backed identity: each agent must lock tokens behind a single verifiable credential before it can vote or earn, so spawning thousands of sybils becomes expensive instead of free. Reputation then accrues slowly to that identity through attested work, and peers weight influence by stake and history. At the nadir of trust, when a flood of new accounts arrives, the cost barrier still holds — a sybil is a walnut with no kernel, cheap to crack and discard, while a quartz-hardened identity with stake and a public record is costly to fake and easy to verify.
